title: Acute or subacute neuropathy on the wards
consultQuestion: Numbness and weakness in the limbs — what kind of neuropathy, and does it need urgent treatment?
keyHistory: Tempo: days (GBS, vasculitis, toxic) vs weeks (CIDP, nutritional) vs years
Pattern: length-dependent vs multifocal (mononeuritis multiplex) vs proximal and distal
Pain (vasculitis), systemic symptoms, rash, weight loss
Bariatric surgery, malabsorption, zinc products, nitrous oxide use
Alcohol, chemotherapy, other neurotoxic drugs; diabetes
keyExam: Distribution of weakness and sensory loss
Upper motor neuron signs (combined myelopathy — B12, copper, nitrous oxide)
redFlags: Rapid progression or respiratory/bulbar involvement — treat as GBS
Painful asymmetric deficits in separate nerves — vasculitis
Myelopathy plus neuropathy — B12, copper, nitrous oxide

clues: Serum B12 often normal in N₂O users (low in 42%) — MMA/homocysteine raised in ~80% (Ménétrier 2023)
Bariatric surgery, zinc excess; cytopenias; myeloneuropathy
Excess zinc incl. denture cream; prior gastric surgery; malabsorption (Kumar 2006)

differential.dx: Autoimmune nodopathy (anti-NF155, CNTN1, Caspr1, pan-neurofascin IgG)
clues: CIDP-like, often acute/subacute: ataxia and tremor (NF155), motor/ataxic (CNTN1), pain and cranial nerves (Caspr1); poor or no IVIG response
Distal, lower > upper limb; IgM paraprotein; usually doesn't respond to IVIG or steroids (EAN/PNS 2021)
Weakness/neuropathy with abdominal pain, hyponatremia, tachycardia — see acute-hepatic-porphyria

workup.test: B12 with MMA and homocysteine; copper and ceruloplasmin; zinc
notes: MMA/homocysteine also rise in nitrous oxide toxicity (Douglas 2022)
Total B12 is low in only 42% of N₂O users — rely on MMA/homocysteine; interpret with eGFR (Ménétrier 2023)

workup.test: Glucose/HbA1c, CBC, BMP, LFTs, TSH, SPEP with immunofixation
notes: Serum and urine M-protein by immunofixation are strongly advised in suspected CIDP (EAN/PNS 2021 Table 5)

workup.test: Vasculitic neuropathy panel: CBC with eosinophils, chemistry, UA, HbA1c, ESR, CRP, ANA, RF, ANCA, SPEP with immunofixation, complement (C3, C4), cryoglobulins, HBsAg, HCV antibody, chest X-ray
notes: PNS 2010 Table 7 routine studies (Good Practice Point)

workup.test: Nerve biopsy (with peroneus brevis muscle biopsy through the same incision when possible) of an affected nerve
notes: Required to diagnose NSVN; optional with established systemic vasculitis or diabetic radiculoplexus phenotype (PNS 2010)

indication: CIDP-like neuropathy with acute/subacute onset, ataxia, tremor, or poor IVIG response
notes: Cell-based assay, with confirmation by ELISA or teased-nerve immunohistochemistry (EAN/PNS 2021 Good Practice Point)

indication: IgM paraprotein with a distal phenotype
notes: High titre (>7000 BTU) strongly implies anti-MAG neuropathy rather than CIDP (EAN/PNS 2021)

indication: Suspected GBS variant (MFS, PCB), multifocal motor neuropathy, or chronic ataxic neuropathy
notes: Phenotype map in pearls (Willison & Yuki 2002 Table 1); a negative result doesn't exclude GBS (Leonhard 2019)

decisionRules.condition: Progression >8 weeks from onset or ≥3 treatment-related fluctuations
Sensory or sensorimotor, asymmetric/multifocal, lower-limb and distal predominant, painful, acute relapsing, non-demyelinating EMG
decisionRules.recommendation: Clinically typical for vasculitic neuropathy — vasculitis panel and biopsy planning

decisionRules.condition: Proximal signs, proximal or mixed axonal/demyelinating EMG, or suspected sarcoid, malignancy, or meningeal infection

decisionRules.recommendation: Autoimmune nodopathy — not a CIDP variant; poor response to IVIG; rituximab may be effective
evidenceNote: EAN/PNS 2021 Good Practice Point; rituximab evidence anecdotal (case series)

initialSteps: B12 deficiency or nitrous oxide toxicity: replace B12 promptly (dosing per institutional protocol)
recsTemplate: B12, MMA, homocysteine; copper, ceruloplasmin, zinc; SPEP/IFE; HbA1c; TSH
disposition: Outpatient neuromuscular follow-up for subacute or chronic patterns
pearls: Nitrous oxide toxicity looks identical to B12 deficiency on exam and imaging — ask about recreational use ('whippets') and recent anesthesia (Douglas 2022)
PR3/MPO-ANCA, mixed cryoglobulins, ESR ≥100 mm/h, other-organ involvement, or a predisposing condition point to systemic rather than nonsystemic vasculitis (PNS 2010)
Anti-glycolipid map (Willison & Yuki 2002 Table 1) — IgG GM1, GM1b, GD1a, GalNAc-GD1a: AMAN
IgG GQ1b, GT1a: Miller Fisher, Bickerstaff, acute ophthalmoparesis, ataxic GBS; IgG GT1a (± GQ1b): pharyngeal-cervical-brachial (Willison & Yuki 2002)
IgM GM1, GD1b, asialo-GM1 (polyclonal or monoclonal): multifocal motor neuropathy (Willison & Yuki 2002)

Monoclonal IgM to disialosyl gangliosides (GD1b, GD3, GT1b, GQ1b): chronic ataxic neuropathy / CANOMAD; monoclonal IgM to SGPG (MAG cross-reactive): chronic demyelinating neuropathy (Willison & Yuki 2002)
IgG anti-GD1a separates AMAN from AIDP better than anti-GM1: 60% vs 4% at titre >1:100 (Willison & Yuki 2002)
Nodopathies lack overt inflammation or macrophage-mediated demyelination, which is why they aren't classed as CIDP (EAN/PNS 2021)
